metadata.title: 2017 state wage input audit, Jan 1reference
metadata.scenario: general non-tipped adult FLSA-covered hypothetical job; no newly offered employer healthcoverage
metadata.date_convention: Freeze reference hourly wage at Jan 1,2017 for a clearly labeled annualized scenario; this is not a month-by-month2017 wage path. Maine's effective date is resolved: 7 January 2017 (IB 2015, c. 2), as the updates record.
metadata.amount_semantics: source-verified general headline rate under stated coverage category; may require employer/region selection. Never fill null reference_hourly implicitly.
metadata.verified_semantics: amount supported by opened government source for stated generalcategory, not verification of all local/industry exceptions; ME verified true, effective 7 January 2017.
updates: 2026-11-16: added Maryland's 1 July 2017 rate (9.25) and New York's rest-of-state 31 December 2017 rate (10.40) as dated variants, and resolved Maine's effective date as 7 January 2017 from the session law (ME now verified). Sources and access dates in evidence.md; excerpts in sources/.
2026-11-17: replaced two stale Maine notes in date_convention and verified_semantics, which still called its date a conflict, with its resolved 7 January 2017 date; no rate or date changed.

ME.name: Maine
ME.locator: 2014–2019 table, 2017 column; Hawaii Table12.43, PDF pages57–58
ME.verification_level: session law effective date (Laws of Maine, IB 2015, c. 2) and contemporaneous Maine DOL releases
notes: General adult non-tipped state-law rate, with federal 7.25 floor for FLSA-covered employment; excludes local/industry/youth/training exceptions.

StrictJan 1 reference is7.50; contemporaneous agency material and DOLdatedtable make9.00 effectiveJan 7. Current codified text saysJan 1, so legal-date conflict needs explicit decision/confirmation before a national Jan 1run.

Resolved 2026-11-16: the initiated act that enacted the 9.00 rate, IB 2015, c. 2 (I.B. 4, L.D. 1661), is printed in the Laws of Maine with 'Effective January 7, 2017.' Its amended text of 26 MRSA §664(1) says 'Starting January 1, 2017', but the act could not operate before it took effect. The Maine DOL release of 15 December 2016 gives 'Effective date: Jan. 7, 2017 (30 days after the Governor has certified the election results).' Both accessed 2026-11-16. The 2017 path is 7.50 for 6 days and 9.00 for 359 days.

variants.locator: IB 2015, c. 2, Laws of Maine page 947: 'Effective January 7, 2017.'; Maine DOL release 15 December 2016: 'Effective date: Jan. 7, 2017'

Added 2026-11-16: Md. Code, Lab. & Empl. §3-413(c) as enacted by 2014 Laws of Maryland ch. 262 (HB 295) sets 8.75 for the 12-month period beginning 1 July 2016 and 9.25 for the 12-month period beginning 1 July 2017 (accessed 2026-11-16). Corroborated by the DLS 2017 fiscal note on HB 317 and by the existing-law text in 2019 SB 280. The 2017 path is 8.75 for 181 days and 9.25 for 184 days.
